text: Which cabinets can be combined in one row, how many per row, and is there a maximum row length? Today a cabinet joins a row when its bottom is level with the row and its edge touches the row end; overlapping placements are shown in red and cannot be applied.

text: Maximum length. Today each collection (for example Urban Low Height) has a maximum length that comes from the countertop. With modular Drag & Drop, cabinets can also be placed without a countertop over them, so that limit no longer covers every case. We assume the countertop limit stays the main rule. What is the maximum length and the maximum number of rows for cabinets that are not under the main countertop: when the countertop is remote, or when cabinets sit below it?
heading: Drag & Drop and movement

text: Correct: the countertop limit stays the main rule

text: For cabinets not under a main countertop (e.g., OS cabs), there is no designated limit.

text: Countertop and sink
heading: Countertop and sink

text: If the countertop is freestanding (not attached to a cabinet), should the sink be positioned along the length of the countertop? If so, are there any restrictions, such as a minimum distance from the edges of the countertop? (This also seems to be a new rule; it wasn't mentioned before.)
heading: Countertop and sink

text: Integrated Countertop Style
heading: Countertop and sink

text: The edge of an integrated basin cannot be within 10cm of the edge of the countertop. See the rule here
heading: Countertop and sink

text: Vessel Countertop Styles
heading: Countertop and sink

text: The vessel hole cutout cannot be within 15” of the countertop edge
heading: Countertop and sink

text: Exceptions are for countertops shorter than 32” in length
heading: Countertop and sink

text: The vessel hole must always be centered on the countertop in these applications
heading: Countertop and sink

text: How does the price of a multi-row configuration differ from that of a single-row one?
heading: Pricing

text: The only changes are the additional countertop(s) that get applied on top of the applicable cabinets (SC cabinet types)
heading: Pricing

text: How is the price of cabinets determined if they are not located under a countertop? If such a cabinet is covered on top by a top panel (decorative panel) instead of a countertop, is this panel considered a separate element that is priced separately? And how does the presence of a countertop above them affect the price?
heading: Pricing

text: Yes, the countertop (decorative panel) would be a separate element, its own SKU. We use the same SKU structure. See that here in the other GDoc
